title: Recursion and the call stack
objective: Watch the call stack grow as a function calls itself, and unwind as the answers come back.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): recursion and divide-and-conquer

simplifies: Python limits how deep the call stack can go (about 1,000 calls by default), so very deep recursion fails. A loop does the same job here without that limit.

quiz.prompt: What stops a recursive function from calling itself forever?

options.text: A base case that returns without calling again
options.explanation: Right. Here n <= 1 returns 1 straight away.

options.text: The computer runs out of time
options.explanation: Without a base case it would run out of stack space and crash, not stop cleanly.
Python allows far more; the base case is what stops it.

quiz.prompt: fact(5) calls fact(4), which calls fact(3)… Which call finishes first?

options.explanation: Right. The last call made is the first to return: last in, first out, like a stack.
fact(5) finishes last: it waits for everything below it.
Each waits for the one it called, so they finish in reverse order.
